title: Captain Quorum and the Motion to Adjourn
author: Civic Morale Directorate (uncredited)
blurb: A pre-Collapse civic title about a man whose superpower is procedure. Printed on paper better than anything made since, in flat confident colours, by an office that wanted you to feel a very particular way about committees. Read now, it is either the funniest thing in the shop or the most frightening, and the shop’s proprietor will not tell you which.
source: Scanned from the Mint Condition reading copy, Ironside Street, Coldwater. In-universe fiction.

chapters.title: Part One — A Point of Order
chapters.text:
PANEL ONE. A civic hall, drawn in the clean confident line of a company that had a studio and a deadline and no opinions. Bunting. A raised dais. Two hundred citizens in the seats, and not one of them has a face — this is not a stylistic choice made for horror, it is a stylistic choice made for budget, and eighty years later it does the horror for free.

On the dais: CAPTAIN QUORUM. Sash, cape, gavel. Square jaw. Colour palette: municipal green and municipal gold.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Friends! Neighbours! Ratepayers!

CROWD: HOORAY!

PANEL TWO.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: The Directorate has proposed a THIRD RESERVOIR for our growing city!

CROWD: HOORAY!

PANEL THREE. A figure stands up in the third row. He has a face. He is the only person in the entire issue apart from Quorum who has a face, and it is a weaselly one, and he is drawn in a colour that appears nowhere else on the page: a sour purple.

DISSENTER: And who's paying for it?

PANEL FOUR. The crowd turns. Two hundred blank ovals, all rotated fifteen degrees.

CAPTION: A hush fell over the hall. For into every civic process, sooner or later, there comes... A POINT OF ORDER!

PAGE TWO.

PANEL ONE. Quorum raises the gavel. There are speed lines. There is a small starburst. It is, and there is no way around this, a superhero panel about a man raising a gavel.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: I recognise the gentleman!

DISSENTER: I said WHO'S PAYING —

CAPTAIN QUORUM: The gentleman is RECOGNISED, and the gentleman has THREE MINUTES!

PANEL TWO. A clock appears in the corner of the panel. It will remain in the corner of every panel for the next nine pages. This is either the cheapest or the cleverest device in pre-Collapse comics and the answer is that it is both.

PANEL THREE.

DISSENTER: My family has drawn water from the Marrow cut for four generations —

CAPTION: 2:41

PANEL FOUR.

DISSENTER: — and now they tell us the cut is to be capped, and the reservoir is to be METERED, and a METER is to be fitted in every KITCHEN —

CAPTION: 2:09

PANEL FIVE. Quorum, in the foreground, back to us, gavel resting on his shoulder like a bat. Perfectly relaxed.

CAPTION: 1:52

PAGE THREE.

PANEL ONE.

DISSENTER: — and I say, I SAY, that a city that measures its people will one day BILL them for existing, and I say the reservoir is not a gift, it is a LEDGER, and I say —

CAPTION: 0:14

PANEL TWO. The dissenter stops. He looks at the clock.

PANEL THREE. He looks at the two hundred blank ovals.

PANEL FOUR.

CAPTION: 0:00

PANEL FIVE. Quorum turns around. Big grin. All teeth.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Thank you! The gentleman's time has expired! The gentleman may submit the remainder IN WRITING!

CROWD: HOORAY!

PAGE FOUR.

PANEL ONE. The dissenter sits down.

PANEL TWO. The dissenter is still sitting down.

PANEL THREE. The chair beside him is empty and we did not see anybody leave.

PANEL FOUR. Wide. Quorum, arms spread, cape out, the whole hall behind him.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: THE MOTION CARRIES!

CROWD: HOORAY!

CAPTION: And so, thanks to the tireless vigilance of CAPTAIN QUORUM, the business of the city was CONCLUDED — in FORTY-ONE MINUTES!

CAPTION: A NEW RECORD!

chapters.title: Part Two — The Motion to Adjourn
chapters.text:
PANEL ONE. A back room. Smaller, browner, no bunting. Three figures at a table, all blank-faced, all in the same municipal green.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: Captain, the gentleman submitted in writing.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Splendid! The system WORKS!

PANEL TWO. A document is slid across the table. We see it side-on: it is very thick.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: He submitted four hundred pages.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Ah.

PANEL THREE. Close on Quorum. First time in the issue his jaw is not square.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: Under Standing Order Eleven, a written submission must be READ INTO THE RECORD.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: In FULL.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: By the CHAIR.

PANEL FOUR. Quorum, magnificently, straightens his sash.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Then I shall read.

PAGE SIX.

PANEL ONE. The hall. Empty seats. One figure on the dais, reading aloud.

CAPTION: He read for six hours.

PANEL TWO. Same composition. The light through the high windows has moved.

CAPTION: He read for eleven.

PANEL THREE. Same composition. Dark outside. A lamp on the lectern.

CAPTION: He read for nineteen.

PANEL FOUR. Same composition. Light again.

CAPTION: The Standing Orders did not provide for a recess. This was not an oversight. Captain Quorum had drafted them himself, in a happier year, and he had been very proud of that clause, and he had explained it to a great many people at a great many functions.

PAGE SEVEN.

PANEL ONE. Close. His voice is drawn as a thin wavering balloon line, which the studio used for radios and for the dying.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: "— and I say that a city that measures its people will one day bill them for existing —"

PANEL TWO.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: "— and I say the reservoir is not a gift, it is a ledger —"

PANEL THREE. He stops. He is looking at the page.

PANEL FOUR. The page. We see it. It is the same paragraph again.

PANEL FIVE. He turns over. It is the same paragraph again.

PANEL SIX. He turns over. It is the same paragraph again.

PAGE EIGHT.

PANEL ONE. Four hundred pages, fanned across the dais floor. Every one identical.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: ... he only wrote it once.

PANEL TWO. Wide, from the back of the hall. One small green figure alone on a dais, surrounded by paper, in a building with nobody in it.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: He only wrote it once and I have said it four hundred times.

PANEL THREE. The doors at the back of the hall. Shut.

PANEL FOUR. Close on the gavel, on the lectern, where he has put it down.

PAGE NINE.

PANEL ONE. He picks it up.

PANEL TWO. He raises it.

PANEL THREE. Full page. The gavel coming down, speed lines, starburst, the whole apparatus of a superhero landing a blow — and the caption, in the same cheerful municipal lettering as every caption in the book:

CAPTION: "The Chair moves that this meeting be ADJOURNED."

CAPTION: There being no objection —

CAPTION: — and there being nobody present to object —

CAPTION: — the motion CARRIES.

PAGE TEN.

PANEL ONE. The empty hall.

PANEL TWO. The empty hall.

PANEL THREE. The empty hall, and on the far wall, low, half-hidden behind a stack of folded chairs, a small painted-over cabinet with a little glass window.

CAPTION: NEXT MONTH: CAPTAIN QUORUM in "A FRIENDLY AMENDMENT"!

CAPTION: Ask your newsagent to reserve your copy!

—

[Inside back cover:] CIVIC MORALE DIRECTORATE. Printed by authority. Not to be sold above the cover price. Not to be defaced. Not to be retained after the period of currency.
